# pbs_services (Data Source)

Lists the system services of a Proxmox Backup Server node and their state, as the Services panel of its interface shows them. PBS reports a fixed set of services, always in this order: `proxmox-backup` (the API server), `proxmox-backup-proxy` (the proxy that serves the web interface and the API on port 8007), `sshd`, `systemd-journald`, `cron`, `postfix` and `chrony`. A service that is not installed is still listed, with `unit_state` `not-found`.

PBS asks systemd, with `systemctl show`, and leaves out a service systemd cannot show. A node without systemd, such as PBS in a Docker container, therefore reports no services: `services` is an empty list then, not an error.

Needs `Sys.Audit on /system/services`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "pbs_services" "this" {}

# The state of each service by its ID, such as
# { "proxmox-backup-proxy" = "running", "chrony" = "running", ... }; empty on
# PBS in a container without systemd.
output "service_states" {
  value = { for s in data.pbs_services.this.services : s.service => s.state }
}

# Warn when the clock is not kept in sync: certificates, sign-in tickets and
# TOTP codes depend on it. A node without systemd lists no services, and
# passes.
check "pbs_time_sync_is_running" {
  assert {
    condition = alltrue([
      for s in data.pbs_services.this.services : s.state == "running" if s.service == "chrony"
    ])
    error_message = "chrony is not running on the PBS node."
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `node` (String) Node to read: `localhost` or the node's host name. Defaults to the provider's `node`.

### Read-Only

- `services` (Attributes List) The services, in PBS's fixed order; empty on a node without systemd. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--services))

<a id="nestedatt--services"></a>
### Nested Schema for `services`

Read-Only:

- `description` (String) Description of the unit, as systemd reports it, such as `Proxmox Backup API Proxy Server`.
- `name` (String) Name of the service as PBS reports it. PBS takes it from a `Name` property that `systemctl show` does not print, so it is the same as `service` — `sshd`, say, not the `ssh.service` unit it is an alias of.
- `service` (String) ID of the service in PBS, one of those above, such as `proxmox-backup-proxy`.
- `state` (String) State of the unit: systemd's sub-state, such as `running`, `exited`, `dead` or `failed`; for a oneshot unit that is not running, the result of its last run instead, such as `success` or `exit-code`. `unknown` when systemd reports none.
- `unit_state` (String) State of the unit's file, which says whether the unit starts at boot: `enabled`, `disabled`, `static`, `masked` and so on, or `not-found` when the unit is not installed. `unknown` when systemd reports none.
